#1296. New Nuno Tavares injury to force Lazio star out of Portugal squad

Lazio full-back Nuno Tavares has been forced to withdraw from the Portugal squad for the Nations League following an injury sustained in the 1-1 draw with Napoli.

The former Arsenal man had been in the starting XI for Sunday’s stalemate at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

He was replaced at half-time due to a muscular problem and it seems to be more serious than previously thought.

According to Sky Sport Italia, Lazio medical staff require further tests to see the extent of the damage, but it is already enough to rule him out of international duty with Portugal.

The 26-year-old played in all 11 Serie A games for leaders Lazio this season, contributing a goal and four assists.

Nuno Tavares only has five senior caps for Portugal since making his debut in November 2024, the most recent was on October 4, 2026.

His career has been beset by repeated injury problems, most of them muscular, going back to his time at Arsenal, Nottingham Forest and Olympique Marseille.

#1295. Leeds defender Jayden Bogle victim of racial abuse online after escaping red card for challenge on Tottenham's Mathys Tel

Published: 14:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 18:15 EST, 8 November 2026

Jayden Bogle has been racially abused online after Leeds’ Premier League win over Tottenham on Saturday.

His club have promised to push for ‘the strongest possible action’ if those responsible for the posts can be identified.

Leeds’ statement read: ‘Leeds United are appalled at the disgusting, racist social media abuse Jayden Bogle suffered following Saturday’s Premier League victory against Tottenham Hotspur.

‘Leeds United condemns this behaviour in the strongest possible terms. There is no place for racism in football or society.

‘The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them.

‘Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his team-mates, and we all stand with him at this time. Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse.’

Jayden Bogle has been the victim of sickening racial abuse after avoiding a red card for this challenge against Tottenham on Saturday

Leeds have promised to push for legal action to be taken against the abusers if they can be identified

Along with the racist and highly offensive messages, the posts, believed to have come from four separate accounts, featured emojis of monkeys and bananas.

Bogle was involved in a controversial incident during the Tottenham game. The 26-year-old escaped a red card when his studs made heavy contact with the ankle of Mathys Tel, forcing the Spurs player to go off injured.

After the game, Leeds boss Daniel Farke said: ‘Jayden is one of the fairest players in the country.

He is more like a butterfly than an eagle and he would not even foul a player on purpose, let alone injure them. It was never intentional and maybe this is why the VAR said it was not a red card.’

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi is reportedly unconvinced by key midfield duo James Maddison and Conor Gallagher, identifying Nottingham Forest star Morgan Gibbs-White as a major transfer target to revamp his engine room.

According to a report by TEAMtalk journalist Graeme Bailey, De Zerbi has raised internal questions regarding his existing central options at North London.

The Italian tactician is reportedly not yet convinced that either Maddison or Gallagher will be key part of his long-term tactical vision at Spurs.

De Zerbi is understood to be seeking a different type of creative midfielder who can thrive in his demanding, possession-based system.

Tottenham have maintained a long-standing admiration for Gibbs-White after failing in their initial pursuit to sign the midfielder last year.

De Zerbi is reportedly particularly keen on bringing the 26-year-old England international to Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as he looks to inject world-class creative spark into his squad.

As per the report, Spurs believe Gibbs-White would be open to a move to North London, though no formal club-to-club agreement has been struck yet with Nottingham Forest.

Gibbs-White’s potential arrival would represent a transformative signing for Tottenham’s midfield architecture.

The 26-year-old creator has established himself as one of the Premier League’s most effective playmakers at Forest.

Statistically, Gibbs-White consistently ranks among the top midfielders in Europe for key metrics.

In the 180 games he has played for Nottingham Forest, he has provided an incredible 37 goals and 38 assists.

That represents a combined 75 goal contributions, averaging approximately one direct goal involvement every 2.4 matches.

However, signing Gibbs-White would not automatically mean Maddison or Gallagher leaving the club.

Tottenham’s eventual plans will depend on De Zerbi’s assessment of his squad, the availability of potential targets and the financial demands of any deal.

#1293. All 160 Serie A players on international duty in November

A total of 160 Serie A players will join up with their national team sides during the November international break: Here is a reminder of who they all are.

The November international break officially kicks off today (Monday, November 9) and will run until next Sunday (November 22). Italy will be in Nations League action against France in San Siro on Thursday and away against Belgium in Brussels on Sunday.

Of Mancini’s current Italy national team squad, 24 of them currently play their football in Serie A. Gianluigi Donnarumma, Riccardo Calafiori, Honest Ahanor, Michael Kayode, Marco Palestra, Issa Doumbia, Sandro Tonali and Luca Koleosho are the only members of the Azzurri squad not currently playing in Italy.

Inter have provided the most Italy internationals this break with Alessandro Bastoni, Federico Dimarco, Nicolo Barella and Pio Esposito. Atalanta and Como have provided three Italy internationals apiece.

Inter also have the most senior international players in November with 14, followed by Atalanta, Como and Roma with 12 apiece, Udinese with 11, and then Juventus and Torino with 10 apiece.

Manchester United are reportedly interested in signing Juventus defender Andrea Cambiaso as they continue to explore options to strengthen their full-back positions ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

According to a report from TuttoJuve, the Red Devils have expressed interest in the Italian international, who could become a potential replacement for Luke Shaw at Old Trafford.

Manchester United were keen to bring in a new left-back during the summer transfer window, with Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall among their preferred targets. However, INEOS ultimately decided against adding a player in that position.

Michael Carrick’s side remain interested in strengthening their defensive options, and Cambiaso could prove to be an attractive solution. The 26-year-old has established himself as an important player for Juventus and offers considerable versatility.

He is comfortable operating on either side of the defence and can also feature as a wing-back. His ability to contribute in different positions could make him a valuable option for United, particularly given their need for greater depth across the defensive line.

Cambiaso has registered eight goals and 19 assists in 142 appearances for Juventus. He remains under contract with the Italian giants until 2029, meaning United could face a difficult task negotiating his departure.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Meanwhile, uncertainty surrounding Luke Shaw’s long-term future could increase United’s interest in the Juventus defender.

The England international is approaching the final months of his contract, although United are reportedly open to discussing an extension. His injury record, availability and substantial wages could complicate negotiations.

A departure in 2027 remains a possibility, and United may need to identify a suitable long-term replacement.

Cambiaso has the technical ability and positional flexibility to strengthen Carrick’s squad. However, it remains to be seen whether Juventus would consider selling one of their important players.

#1291. Official: Sassuolo have fired Aquilani after five straight defeats

Sassuolo have officially announced the dismissal of coach Alberto Aquilani after five consecutive Serie A defeats, with Roberto D’Aversa the favourite to take over ahead of Vincenzo Montella.

The decision had been in the air following the 3-0 loss to his old club Roma, a result that took his total record on the bench this season to four wins, two draws and seven defeats between Serie A and the Coppa Italia.

This was his first top flight experience as a coach, following roles in Serie B with Pisa and Catanzaro, while before that he was a coach at the Fiorentina youth academy.

Called in to replace Fabio Grosso over the summer, Aquilani had signed a contract to June 2028 and started quite well, the highlight being the 3-2 win over Juventus on September 13.

That was also the last moment of joy, followed by a 1-1 draw against Milan and six defeats.

It is widely reported that Roberto D’Aversa is the favourite to take over, but so far Sassuolo have only announced that Aquilani has been removed from his post.

Another potential candidate is former Turkiye international coach Montella.

That’s weird, I thought they’d already met their season’s goal of playing their hearts out against Milan.

#1290. Man United are a rotten, shambolic mess. They lack intelligence, look uncoached and fumbling, failing Michael Carrick is not the man to arrest this trauma, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 14:32 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 20:25 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United do not have a football team, more a collection of adrenaline junkies. Over time, it will not be enough.

So deficient are Michael Carrick's players that they surely can't keep their manager in a job for much longer. For the most part United are shambolic, a mess. At times they play football so devoid of intelligence and competence that it's almost impossible to fathom. They look uncoached.

Yet here they were for the second night running at Old Trafford, completing a lap of honour at full-time while their supporters sang the name of Carrick as he completed his own journey in front of the Stretford End towards the tunnel.

United – it's worth pointing out – are third bottom of the Premier League. They haven't won in the league since August and have conceded more goals across all competitions – 30 – than any team bar Crystal Palace in Europe's top divisions.

But at Old Trafford they will cling to anything to help them look in the mirror without laughing and currently the currency is comebacks. There was one against Roma in the Champions League last Tuesday and here – quite remarkably – there were two in one game.

None of it should really mean anything in the grand scheme. United are rotten, capable of playing effectively only when something gives them an energy spike with which to roll. It makes for quite hypnotic theatre but has inadequacy and desperation at its core.

Patrick Dorgu (centre) scored a late equaliser as troubled Man United drew 4-4 vs Aston Villa

Dorgu scored in the 96th-minute with this header but United sit 18th in the Premier League

Despite the draw, Michael Carrick's position as United head coach looks increasingly doubtful

It won't sustain them or indeed their fumbling, failing manager. But for the moment it's what they have and what they are.

MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): Lammens 4; Mazraoui 4, Yoro 6, Maguire 5 (Heaven 46, 5), Dalot 3 (Dorgu 66, 8); Tielemans 6 (Mount 66, 5), Mainoo 6; Amad 5 (Lacey 66, 7), Fernandes 6, Cunha 7; Mbeumo 5 (Zirkzee 83, 7)

Goals: Fernandes (16 pen), Tielemans (44), Zirkzee (90+2), Dorgu (90+6)

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 5, Lindelof 6, Torres 6, Maatsen 4; Goretzka 6 (Mbaye 78, 6), Kamara 4; Alysson 7 (Barkley 71, 6), McGinn 8 (Hemmings 71, 6), Manzambi 6; Jackson 6 (Madjo 86)

Goals: Alysson (1), Jackson (4), McGinn (48 pen), Goretzka (53)

Here, they twice trailed by two, at the start of both halves. They were 2-0 down after only four minutes and 4-2 behind after 53. Somehow they managed not to lose.

The two goals United scored in added time at the end of the game came from absolutely nowhere. On the touchline Carrick – free from total humiliation for the second time in six days – raised a single finger to the sky.

In the directors' box – where the TV companies seem to have a camera permanently trained these days – fist pumps were in evidence from those in United blazers.

This was another uncomfortable afternoon for Messrs Ratcliffe, Wilcox and Berrada. A collection of new banners in the crowd made feelings known.

For now, Carrick is being spared any of the blame. That is strange and wrong but tells us much about the confused nature of the modern United. If they blame one of their own then they really do have nowhere left to go in search of self-respect.

United's opening against Roma last week had been traumatic enough. This was even worse but the root of it was desperately familiar – incompetent football.

The hapless United full-back Diogo Dalot was to blame for the first goal as Villa's Brazilian Alysson blasted his shot through the Portuguese's limp challenge. Later – after conceding a second half penalty – Dalot was booed off by his own fans.

That was painful and unedifying but completely understandable. Dalot has played more than 250 games for United yet has never even been good enough.

Aston Villa took the lead after just 59 seconds when Alysson (centre) scored at Old Trafford

Nicolas Jackson (centre) doubled the visitors' lead on four minutes as they made a dream start

Bruno Fernandes pulled one back for the hosts with a penalty on 16 minutes in a crazy start

For goal two, goalkeeper Senne Lammens was culpable as he pushed Alysson's shot into the path of Nicolas Jackson.

Once again United were in sink or swim territory. Once again, amazingly, they kept their heads above water – at least for a while.

Boubacar Kamara's 13th minute challenge on Matheus Cunha was stupid as the Brazilian was heading away from goal. But the Bruno Fernandes penalty that followed was calm and precise and the shot of belief United needed was theirs.

For the next 20 minutes or so, Carrick's team played well off the back of it. It was the only part of their game that will look good on the highlights. The United front four pressed and harried the Villa defence to the extent that Unai Emery's team couldn't get up the field.

Villa keeper Zion Suzuki saved well from a Cunha curler while subsequent shots from Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Amad Diallo took deflections and narrowly missed the target.

At some stage it felt as though United's energy must drop. Over time it did. But then they equalised.

Moments after seeing Suzuki save one of his own efforts, Amad found space to pull the ball back for Youri Tielemans who placed his first United goal in from 18 yards against his old club. Carrick's team deserved to be level at that stage and had played some enterprising football to get there. But their self-harm gene surfaced again before long.

Youri Tielemans (right) brought United level before half-time with this strike vs his old club

John McGinn put Villa ahead again just minutes after half-time from the penalty spot

Leon Goretkza (left) made it 4-2 to Villa with this close-range strike as they looked set to win

Joshua Zirkzee (left) pulled one back in second-half stoppage-time with this finish for United

Alysson had almost scored with the last big moment of the first half and in the 47th minute he drew an utterly dumb foul from Dalot and John McGinn scored the penalty firmly.

United are beyond compare in the Premier League when it comes to this kind of thing. Who else in the top flight concedes the kind of goals they do? A case in point came in the 53rd minute.

McGinn's free-kick was heading across goal and away when United defender Leny Yoro inexplicably headed it towards his own goal. Lammens somehow touched the ball on to the bar but when it dropped Leon Goretzka poked it in.

That was the 16th goal United had conceded in the last five games and this time the attempt at a fightback was more muted.

There were some half chances – shots from Cunha and Fernandes – and some territory in which to play.

But this was a game Villa were now able to control rather better and they looked set to ease home until Patrick Dorgu crossed for Joshua Zirkzee to ease a goal in from out of nothing in the 2nd minute of added time.

Old Trafford was emptying fast by the time Dorgu headed in a 96th equaliser from a corner. But by then the collective blood was up once more and it was enough.

Villa appealed for a foul on goalkeeper Suzuki and it's true Lammens had gone looking for him. Was the contact between the two 'keepers significant enough to warrant VAR intervention? Probably not. United had their draw and they had a point.

If the season ended today, they would be down. Yet they were cheered off. Some things you just can't make up.

Aston Villa have reached a verbal agreement with left-back Ian Maatsen over a new contract to secure his long-term future at Villa Park.

According to a report from Football Insider, Aston Villa have made a major breakthrough in negotiations to tie down the 24-year-old Dutch international.

As per report, Unai Emery and the club’s board have been impressed by Maatsen’s performances and decided that rewarding him with an improved deal was a priority.

Following initial discussions that began back in September, both parties have now reached an agreement in principle.

With verbal terms locked in, all that remains before an official announcement is for final paperwork to be drawn up and signed.

Securing Maatsen’s commitment marks a significant victory for Aston Villa after fighting off late summer transfer interest from Manchester United.

During the closing stages of the August transfer window, Manchester United actively explored a move for the former Chelsea defender to solve their ongoing crisis at left-back.

However, Villa rejected all inquiries and refused to negotiate, standing firm in their stance that Maatsen was fundamental to Emery’s tactical plans.

That resolve has paid off, with Maatsen proving pivotal on the pitch while United continue to struggle defensively.

Maatsen’s performances have reinforced his importance to Villa as they look to compete across multiple competitions.

The left-back provides pace, technical ability and attacking support, qualities that suit Emery’s approach.

A new contract would provide reassurance over Maatsen’s future following the interest he attracted during the summer.

#1288. Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick

Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

That is how far United have, once again, fallen. Fans in the Stretford End unfurled their “Standards” banner, bearing the faces of Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and Bryan Robson.

It was first revealed in December 2021 in Carrick’s final match as interim following Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s sacking. This should be his final game again, under different, more traumatic, circumstances.

If it is, he is going out having made a stand. He dropped Bruno Fernandes for his outspoken comments, aimed directly at Carrick and his tactics, following the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat away to Como on Wednesday.

At 2-0 down here it was telling that Carrick turned to Matheus Cunha when he substituted Youri Tielemans, who had been so terribly slow and ineffective, at half-time. Carrick did not bring on Fernandes. And he did not turn to the captain after, as he made four substitutions, including bringing on 19-year-old Shea Lacey. That said it all.

The television cameras catching Omar Berrada, the United chief executive, shaking his head in the stands as Carrick’s team gave away goals also told its own story. They have two wins from 12 in all competitions and none in eight. They have only beaten newly promoted Ipswich Town, in August, and Azerbaijan minnows Sabah this season. United were so careless it looked like they could not care less.

There was no guarantee, after Como, that Carrick would remain in charge after this game. So, losing and losing so embarrassingly – it was three, it should have been five – has to have obvious consequences. However cherished Carrick is. However much the fans excuse him. Yes, he has not been helped enough, but he has also not been good enough.

Finishing third and qualifying for the Champions League last season has proved to be the kind of bounce a new manager can achieve, after the pressure was relieved by the sacking of Ruben Amorim, rather than something more sustainable. There was always the fear that Carrick, despite his playing pedigree, might be out of his depth in this job. And so it is proving to be. Especially as he has been hung out to dry. Carrick certainly appeared resigned to his fate.

But what is he coaching? What is he trying to do with United? How does he want his team to play? Yes, there are limitations, but they are badly set up, tactically poor, and struggle to build attacks. The players are not responding, but it does not mean Carrick is blameless.

Bournemouth were not just collectively and individually better – and despite how good they are, that is some indictment of United – but better organised. They knew what they were doing, believed in it and relished it as they collected a fourth victory, and a fourth clean sheet in a row, after a slow start under Marco Rose, the new head coach. It was no shock.

The nature of the goals spoke volumes. For the first, a free-kick was needlessly conceded by Ayden Heaven, who endured a particularly difficult game, as he lunged in recklessly, forcing Evanilson to jump out of the way or risk injury.

Justin Kluivert whipped the ball in beyond the far post and it was met by Rayan, who volleyed in low and precise. The Brazilian was unmarked. Carrick protested – at what? – and the Bournemouth supporters sang “you’re getting sacked in the morning”.

What a finish from Rayan to give Bournemouth the lead! 🔥 https://t.co/9BV0G5Tqgi

The outstanding Rayan should have had a hat-trick but failed to take two chances in the second half, when he only had goalkeeper Senne Lammens to beat, after Bournemouth had already doubled their lead. It came as Leny Yoro slipped over and presented the ball straight to Adrien Truffert, who squared it for Marcus Tavernier to side-foot home. It was that ridiculously easy.

The third was the same, with Evanilson chasing down a ball forward by Tyler Adams. The striker should not have got there. But Harry Maguire, captain in Fernandes’s absence, gave up, pointing at Lammens to win it. Bruno Fernandes has been dropped for Manchester United’s crucial Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Michael Carrick has taken the decision to drop the United captain to the bench in the wake of his public criticism on Wednesday following the shambolic 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como.

Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics and has now been taken out of the starting XI.

The move had looked likely with Carrick refusing to rule out stripping Fernandes of the captaincy when quizzed on the matter on Friday.

Carrick had responded to Fernandes questioning the set up and approach by suggesting tactics can go out of the window when players are unprepared to run.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Manchester United vs Bouremouth.

United enter Sunday’s clash against Bournemouth in the grip of a deepening crisis. Wednesday night’s dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat to debutants Como extended United’s’ winless run to seven matches across all competitions - their worst sequence since 2015.

With just one victory from their opening seven Premier League fixtures, United are enduring their worst start to a top-flight season since 1986-87. Head coach Michael Carrick, a multiple champion at Old Trafford during his playing days, finds his position under severe threat, with reports suggesting another defeat could seal his departure. While both of United’s wins this season have come at home, they remain winless in their last three at Old Trafford. On an individual level, Bryan Mbeumo has offered a rare bright spark, scoring four goals in seven league outings while Bruno Fernandes continues to search for form, and the captain’s recent outburst only makes the atmosphere more febrile.

In stark contrast, Bournemouth arrive in Manchester brimming with confidence. Marco Rose’s side have enjoyed a flawless start to their inaugural European campaign, sitting joint-top of the Europa League standings after a dominant 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s ten-man AC Milan on Thursday. That result marked a third consecutive home win and clean sheet, with Bournemouth outscoring opponents 8-0 in that stretch. Midfielder Marcus Tavernier has been instrumental, leading the club’s scoring charts with five goals across 11 appearances.

Bournemouth will feel no trepidation visiting Old Trafford, having gone unbeaten in their last six Premier League meetings with United (two wins, four draws). With Carrick desperate for a stabilising result and Rose’s side riding high on European momentum, today’s fixture carries significant stakes for both clubs.

The 2026 Nature Spotlight: Neuroscience tables are based on the Nature Index database, covering research articles published between 2021 and 2025.

The data are drawn from a subset of 128 journals in the Nature Index that excludes journals in areas unrelated to neuroscience. In 125 of these, neuroscience articles were identified using a combination of search terms, including keywords and fields of interest, in Digital Science’s Dimensions database (Digital Science is part of Holtzbrinck, the majority shareholder of Nature’s publisher, Springer Nature). These extracted articles, plus all of the Nature Index articles in three other journals — the Journal of Neuroscience, Nature Neuroscience and Neuron — formed the data for this spotlight.

#1286. De Bruyne future at Napoli uncertain as possibility of January exit emerges

Kevin De Bruyne is facing an uncertain future at club level, and local reports suggest that the Belgian superstar could potentially even leave as early as January.

De Bruyne has been with Napoli for almost 18 months, having joined on a free transfer at the end of his Manchester City contract in the summer of 2025.

The 35-year-old has started in all 11 of Napoli’s Serie A matches so far this season. This has followed a disappointing 2024-25 season on an individual level, which saw De Bruyne miss over four months of action with a major hamstring injury midway through the campaign.

De Bruyne also found himself wrapped up in controversy at the end of last season, when he said that he was ‘happy’ to see head coach Antonio Conte leave, suggesting that he and the coach had a ‘very different vision of football’, adding “I never had the opportunity to play in my preferred position.”

Conte has since been replaced by Massimiliano Allegri, who has endured a wretched start to his Napoli career. The Partenopei have lost seven of their first 15 matches under Allegri’s stewardship, they are in 10th place in the Serie A table, already 14 points off the league leaders after 11 matches.

They have also lost three of their first four Champions League matches and are currently in 27th place in the European standings, at risk of missing out on qualification to the play-off round. Direct qualification for the round of 16 is already looking impossible.

In spite of his obvious quality and experience, De Bruyne’s first year-and-a-half in Italy have not worked out as well as he would have hoped, and now, there have been suggestions that he could leave as early as January.

Napoli, who had a relatively quiet summer transfer window, are expected to make several moves in January, both in terms of incomings and outgoings: Monday’s reports indicate that Allegri wants at least three or four new additions, and reports over the weekend claimed that Lorenzo Lucca, Noa Lang and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa are among the most likely names to be sacrificed.

Monday’s reports from Il Mattino add that De Bruyne’s future is also uncertain, despite the fact that Allegri has ‘done everything’ to get the Belgian onside. Il Mattino adds that it ‘drastic decisions’ regarding De Bruyne’s future during the January transfer window can not be ruled out at this stage.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

This guy is getting too big for his britches, especially since he is now a shell of his best which was never world class anyway.

#1283. Soccer hooligans descend on Australia: Wild footage shows horde of fans smashing cars and damaging property

Published: 03:01 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 03:27 EST, 9 November 2026

Shocking footage of soccer fans after a match has reignited complaints about public safety, following previous warnings repeated violence was putting families at risk.

Perth Glory supporters have demanded action over a confrontation near HBF Park, with video posted on social media showing a group of young people as they crowded around a parked white vehicle and aggressively rocked it from side to side.

Other footage filmed from across the road shows young people confronting fans in the street, with the group spread across the footpath and roadway outside nearby businesses.

Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions, as well as damaged fences and other property. Supporters allege the material documents a recurring problem involving the same group and have demanded bans and stronger security measures.

The footage prompted calls for bans and renewed criticism of matchday security, with supporters alleging genuine fans face strict enforcement over minor issues while more serious behaviour goes unchecked.

'The same group of troublemakers causing chaos and mobbing random people', one fan posted on social media platform X.

Young people crowd around a parked white car and aggressively rock it near HBF Park in footage that has sparked anger among Perth Glory supporters

Supporters allege genuine fans are being left feeling unsafe at Perth Glory matches

Tagging Perth Glory, they added: 'It's time you do something about it. People have had enough.'

The supporter also called for individuals to be banned and, in a subsequent post, alleged nearby property had been damaged.

WA Police, Perth Glory and A-Leagues have all been contacted for comment.

Perth-based football podcast and digital channel The Far Post Perth shared the original post, adding its own demand for intervention.

'Not a good look at all and something needs to be done about the problem at this point, genuine supporters are being impacted,' the account wrote.

One commenter alleged the group had been moving through the venue during the match while being followed by security and police.

'This is the mob that was walking back and forth all game with security/police following,' they wrote.

'We don't need this at HBF Park. It makes many people feel unsafe when these wannabe thugs just shove their way through.'

Another video shows young people confronting fans on the street outside nearby businesses

Photographs of damaged fences and other property have fuelled calls for stronger action

The person who posted the footage claimed that 'after the game the police and security were nowhere to be seen'.

They also shared a separate video from February, alleging it showed an earlier confrontation involving the same group.

The February post had complained about people attending matches in The Bay supporter area and allegedly fighting with other young spectators.

The complaints follow a strongly worded statement issued last year by supporter groups The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth, which demanded sanctions after a separate incident outside Gate 2 during the second half of a match at HBF Park.

The groups said they were aware of footage circulating online and distanced themselves from those involved, alleging physical confrontations had become a recurring problem.

'We want to make it absolutely clear that those involved are not fans and do not represent our supporter groups, our values, or the wider football community,' their joint statement read.

'These individuals consistently attend matches with the sole intention of causing problems rather than supporting the team, and their behaviour is completely unacceptable.'

The statement alleged confrontations had occurred in active supporter areas and the Eastern family stand, extending the groups' concerns beyond the stadium's most vocal sections.

Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions

'In almost every single game, they have caused physical confrontations in both the Active areas, and in some cases the Eastern family stand too, and it is deeply frustrating that this behaviour continues without meaningful consequences,' the groups said.

They alleged the behaviour was damaging the experience of supporters who attended matches to follow Perth Glory.

The groups also accused matchday security provider NPB Security of failing to respond adequately to incidents.

Their criticism included allegations that a rotating contingent of inexperienced security staff was being deployed and that personnel were unable or unwilling to intervene when serious problems arose.

'The lack of accountability from NPB Security is unacceptable and has undermined the safety of the matchday environment,' the statement read.

'Warnings and passive responses are clearly not working.'

The groups called for bans and other sanctions, warning that further incidents could affect spectators and people working at the ground.

'Without firm action, including bans and real consequences, these so-called 'fans' will continue to put genuine supporters, families, and staff at risk.'

They urged the club and stadium authorities to identify those responsible and impose firm sanctions.

Their earlier warning has been followed by fresh complaints about how security rules are enforced at Perth Glory matches.

'Meanwhile security go OTT about bottled water in the shed or actual fans taking t-shirts off,' one supporter wrote in response to the latest footage.

Another commenter similarly complained that removing a shirt in the supporter bay could result in ejection, while alleging people involved in violence escaped consequences.

The Far Post Perth also challenged a response that dismissed the latest incident as 'kids being kids'.

'Kids being kids is vandalising other people's property? Interesting,' the account replied, referring to the allegations of property damage.

However, one person responding to the original footage questioned whether those shown in the street were Perth Glory supporters.

'In the second video, the person filming is standing where the stadium is. These idiots look like they are walking from the other side of the road,' the commenter wrote.

'Are we sure they are even Glory fans? Or just troublemakers.'

The person who uploaded the footage insisted they were, although the posts do not establish that the same individuals were involved in each of the incidents raised by commenters.

The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth had made their position on violence explicit in their earlier appeal for action.

'Violence, fighting, and antisocial behaviour have no place in football,' they said.

'HBF Park, The Shed, The Bay and all areas of the ground should be a safe and welcoming environment for all supporters, families, players, and staff.'

#1281. Cisse: ‘Italy is full of strong young players, I want to prove I should be here’

Alphadjo Cisse has spoken about the moment he found out he had been called up to the Italy national team for the first time, says that he wants to prove what he has to offer during his first camp with the Nazionale and says that there is plenty of young talent in Serie A and Serie B: ‘Let me tell you’.

Cisse was included in the Italy national team squad for the first time last week, ahead of Nations League fixtures against France on Thursday and Belgium on Sunday.

It has been a remarkable rise to the top for the 20-year-old, who was playing in Serie B with Catanzaro last season. He is now Milan’s leading goalscorer across all competitions in 2026-27 and has already bettered his goalscoring tally from last season with eight from 15 appearances so far.

The versatile attacker spoke in-depth about his career to date and his first Italy call-up in a recent interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio.

The latest Italy squad was announced on Thursday evening, just before Cisse and Milan kicked off against Ferencvaros in the Europa League. Cisse found out that he had been selected for the Azzurri while in the media zone in San Siro.

“I was on my way to do the pre-match interviews ahead of Ferencvaros in the Europa League and they stopped me and said: ‘Alpha, they’ve called you up to the national team … the senior national team!’. I had the game to play, so it only sunk in later,” he recalled (via TMW).

“I want to prove that I should be there. They’d been talking to me about it for about 10 days, but it was still up in the air. This is my big chance. I haven’t had the chance to stop and reflect on my journey here, but football moves quickly!”

Cisse is a glaring example of what can happen when young players are given opportunities at the top level. He feels that there are plenty more uncovered gems knocking about in Serie A and Serie B.

“Italy is full of strong, young players, let me tell you. It just depends on the opportunities you’re given. A lot have come through over the last few months, myself included, and I’m sure that there will be lots more in the near future.

“Once you get to a certain level, it becomes amazing. I was impressed by Pisilli more than anyone: He’s so strong. I knew about him before, but playing with him made me understand his strength.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

Well said Cisse. There is bundles of talent and if they are used along with new infrastructure then Italy will get to the top again.

#1279. Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner

“Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

In truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he said of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”

Kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he said. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”

So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

Kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and said: “You held it together. You got through it.” It showed how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

What a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

Kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

Kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg

For his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

Both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he said. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

Those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

Kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

And he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

That work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and said he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

They probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

Brazilian great Ronaldo, who won this award twice in his career, is on hand to give the award to England striker Harry Kane. The Bayern Munich striker, in his home city, becomes the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001.

“First of all, I am almost speechless. Lucky I have this list. It being in London is extra special and felt like a good omen. Thanks to those who voted for me, as it would have been tough this year. Congratulations to all the nominees and winners tonight.

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

For the 35-time German champions, the award is perhaps even more important than it is for the peerless striker himself. The Bayern hierarchy are planning to travel to the Palladium Theatre en masse to support Kane.

Kane is not only Bayern’s top striker, he is their international figurehead and, internally, their poster-boy professional. Club patron and honorary president Uli Hoeness described the England captain as the best signing in the club’s history. Hoeness even went so far as to say he loves Kane, and he is not alone in this.

There's only one Harry Kane. https://t.co/NfZEFmjaUN

Hoeness is one of many in the club’s leadership who have been endlessly promoting Kane to help the 33-year-old fulfil his lifelong dream of winning the trophy. Bayern officials have been campaigning on his behalf for weeks.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany said: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”

The plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has announced Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before quickly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

#1278. Roma will not release Molina for Argentina duty despite World Cup ban being reduced

Monday’s reports confirm that Roma will not release Nahuel Molina for international duty with Argentina this week, despite his seven-game ban for his antics at the end of the World Cup final being reduced to just four games.

Molina had originally been handed a seven-match ban and a $77,000 fine by FIFA for violent conduct at the end of the 2026 World Cup final, which saw Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 in extra-time. His teammate and former Roma midfielder Leandro Paredes was banned for 10 matches and fined $90,000.

On Saturday, it was confirmed that Molina’s ban had been reduced from seven matches to four, and given that he served the first three games of his suspension during the September-October international break, he now has just one game of his ban left.

Argentina will be involved in two international friendlies during the November international break, against Uruguay and then Costa Rica, and Molina is now eligible to play in the second one of those games.

According to reports Il Messaggero, Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni had attempted to hand Molina a last-minute call-up to the national team squad for the friendlies coming up in November. The latest Argentina squad was announced a few days before Molina’s ban was formally reduced.

However, Roma have reportedly informed the Argentine FA that they will not be releasing Molina for international duty in November, and he is instead expected to report for training with the Giallorossi on Wednesday.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1276. Celtic fans disgracefully boo during minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday: Referee ends tribute after just 13 SECONDS - even after warning from the PA announcer

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:28 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:51 EST, 9 November 2026

Celtic were forced to curtail plans to commemorate Remembrance Day after a section of their supporters booed during the planned minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday.

The Bhoys hosted Kilmarnock in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday - with Liam Scales' goal proving the difference in a 1-0 win.

However, ahead of kick-off at Parkhead, the annual tribute to the armed forces and their families was overshadowed by some fans' loud jeers.

As the players from both teams gathered around the centre-circle, an announcement on the public address system said: 'We will have a minute's silence today on Remembrance Sunday to remember all victims of all conflicts. We remember, in particular, the men who served Celtic football club and lost their lives at wartime.'

The audible disdain resulted in referee John Beaton being forced to cut the silence after just 13 seconds.

The noise was so palpable that the Celtic TV broadcast turned down the volume to try and minimise its impact too.

The minute's silence ahead of Celtic versus Kilmarnock was cut short due to some fans booing

Celtic TV turned down the volume to try and minimise the jeers during the curtailed silence

Referee John Beaton (right) cut the minute's silence after 13 seconds as a result of the booing

Furthermore, the lower tier of the standing section was empty until the Green Brigade and other fans started to file in from the concourse when referee Beaton’s whistle signalled the end of the tribute.

Football clubs across the United Kingdom observe a minute's silence with their nearest home fixture around Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day - with the latter on November 11.

Many teams also wear poppies, something Kilmarnock wore on their strip, but Celtic didn't.

Some Celtic supporters refuse to partake in the tradition or actively take a stance against it, often citing the club’s Irish roots and linking it to the British Army‘s role in The Troubles.

Last season, in a quirk, Celtic hosted Kilmarnock on Remembrance Sunday too - with that minute's silence also cut short due to jeering. That time referee Don Robertson cut it short at 15 seconds.

As well as the booing in that match last term, some fans turned their back on the minute's silence and also made gestures.

Sunday's 1-0 win over Kilmarnock sees Celtic regain their four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership.

It was under-pressure Martin O'Neill's side's first league win in their last three games.

Scales scored the only goal of the game on 26 minutes when he hooked a Camilo Duran cross into the top corner.

Celtic fans show their displeasure during the minute's silence for Remembrance Day in 2025

Celtic - and Kasper Hogh in particular - otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty.

Hogh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without a goal hit the 16-game mark since he netted a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

Celtic have 31 points from their opening 13 matches - four more than bitter rivals Rangers who sit second but have a game in hand.

Kilmarnock remain rooted to the bottom of the table with nine points from 13 games - two adrift of 11th-place Aberdeen who have played a match fewer.

#1275. Football Italia Show: What we learned from Mancini’s press conference

Roberto Mancini has outlined his plans for Italy ahead of two tough fixtures against France and Belgium, stressing the need to develop young talent while balancing experience in the national team. Watch our video from Coverciano to learn what we learned at today’s press conference.

The coach is keen to assess several emerging players, including Alphadjo Cisse and Mattia Liberali. Mancini believes the next generation can bring fresh energy and quality to the Azzurri, although patience and consistent development remain essential.

He also discussed Nicolò Zaniolo, stressing the need for greater consistency and a stronger contribution in attacking positions. Federico Chiesa remains part of his plans, but must first regain full fitness and regular playing time.

Another key issue is Italy’s search for a natural regista following the absence of a specialist capable of controlling the midfield in the traditional Italian style.

Mancini also emphasised the importance of building a united squad and improving the team’s overall identity.

The upcoming matches against France and Belgium will provide valuable opportunities to evaluate the squad and measure Italy’s progress.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

#1274. He Played With Man Utd Icon David Beckham - Now He’s 20x Richer Than Both

David Beckham is among the richest individuals in football but his wealth pales in comparison to a former Premier League star's staggering net worth.

The former Manchester United midfielder has become an entrepreneur since hanging up his boots in 2013 and took on his main business venture a year later. He exercised an option to take a Major League Soccer club to Miami and in 2018 his wish was granted as Inter Miami were launched as MLS' 25th club.

Beckham is one of many legendary footballers who have turned to entrepreneurship post-retirement and many of them have been far more successful as a business person. That's the case for one of his former teammates whose net worth has reached an unimaginable level.

Beckham saw out his career in the USA with LA Galaxy before becoming a co-owner of Inter Miami, but he spent most of his playing days in Europe. His time in Italy came with AC Milan, where he played with big names, including Brazilian icon Ronaldinho.

Former Arsenal midfielder Mathieu Flamini linked up with Beckham in Milan, spending five years with the Rossoneri before returning to the Emirates in 2016. The Frenchman didn't quite reach the heights of England's former captain but he has more than outperformed the former England captain with his business venture.

Back in 2025, The Sunday Times Rich List reported that Beckham and his wife Victoria had a combined net worth of £500 million. That wealth came from not only the Miami expansion but other ventures.

Flamini only needed one to accumulate a remarkable net worth of £10 billion and that came through GFBiochemicals, a biochemical company he founded in 2008. Specialising in producing levulinic acid, this reduces CO2 emissions in manufacturing processes for items such as detergents by as much as 80 percent.

The former France midfielder is GF Biochemicals' chief executive and co-founder, which also helps create substitutes for fossil-based materials and is a leader in environmental sustainability. His astonishing riches have come after a relatively well-paid career in football where, during his time at Arsenal, he won three FA Cups and played in the 2006 Champions League final.

Flamini's post-playing career success hasn't been born out of luck or connections, as he has always held a special connection with the environment. He explained this during an interview with Harvard Business Review in June of this year:

"Football was a childhood dream but the environment has always played an important role in my life. Having grown up in the South of France, I’ve always felt close to nature and the sea. When I was a child, I remember watching documentaries with my family and picking up plastic waste on the beaches."

Flamini added: "I developed an environmental awareness at a very early age. Even during my football career, I wondered how we could find solutions to global warming, and considered the impact humans can have on the environment, but also on their own health."

It was during his time at the San Siro when the Frenchman first saw a path towards becoming a businessman: "When I joined AC Milan at 24, I was one of the youngest players on the squad. Many of my team-mates were already involved in other ventures, which led me to start thinking about entrepreneurship at a very early stage."

He added: "Then there were encounters and opportunities that steered me towards the chemical sector. We developed partnerships with universities in Italy, we met scientists and engineers, and a research group was set up."

Flamini saw a gap in the market which he delved into: "At some point, we decided to focus on a molecule identified by the US Department of Energy as one of the 12 molecules of the future. It showed great potential to replace many petroleum-derived molecules and thus accelerate the transition to a more sustainable chemical industry. However, this platform molecule, levulinic acid, had not yet been developed on an industrial scale. There was therefore a real opportunity here."

Some people's businesses have helped them earn billions after retiring.

The 42-year-old is the second-richest footballer of all time, sitting behind Brunei royal family member Faiq Bolkiah, but he ranks above Beckham, Cristiano Ronaldo and David Beckham. It's an astonishing story and makes him one of the richest self-made former athletes in history.

#1273. Cisse: ‘Practically on the flight to PSV before Milan called, never had any doubt about my quality’

Alphadjo Cisse has spoken in-depth about his rapid rise to the top of Italian football, his life before becoming a professional and the fact that he had been on the verge of signing for PSV Eindhoven before receiving a call from Milan during the January transfer window.

Within the space of just a few months, Cisse has gone from playing his first full season in Serie A to being a hotly-anticipated member of the Italy national team squad and is currently Milan’s leading goalscorer in both Serie A and across all competitions.

The 20-year-old, spoke about his rapid ascent to the top of the Italian pyramid in a recent interview with Cronache di Spohgliatoio.

Going back to where it all began, Cisse said: “My life changed when I was working in my father’s factory. A manager from Verona went to look for him to beg him to take me there. He’s always been a hard worker: Every day at 5 pm, he took a break from work and at 5:15 he’d be in front of the house calling me to take me to play football.

“I still remember the first time. It was in the afternoon, he came up to the house and said: ‘Come on, I’ve got somewhere to take you’. Then we went out onto the pitch. He was the one who passed down my passion for football, and from that moment, I’ve never stopped.”

Cisse feels that he still has plenty of growing up to do in a football sense, though.

“A few weeks ago they asked me how much of myself I’d shown as a footballer and I answered 70%. Maybe I have to lower that a little bit. Let’s say 40%, because I have to improve in many aspects. But, at the same time, I know who I am and what I’m worth.

“Last season Alberto Aquilani, who was my coach at Catanzaro, told me ‘if you don’t play for at least 10 years in Serie A, for me, you will have failed’. I took that as a positive piece of encouragement, and that sentence pushed me to do better and made me believe in the things I can do.”

There was plenty of young Italian talent in last season’s Catanzaro squad, including another fresh face in the Italy squad: Mattia Liberali. Costantino Favasuli also left Catanzaro to join Napoli over the summer.

“Favasuli is one of my best friends in football,” said Cisse. “I met him in Serie B last year. We often found ourselves talking and dreaming together. He once told me ;think about the day when we will be playing for two great teams. It would be great to play in Serie A, but I’m 23, maybe it’s too late for me’. But, he’s done it too. Milan vs. Napoli will be in December, so we’ll see how that goes.

“He was my driver, he would take me to training. He’s an example that there is no age limit to stop feeling young or to stop believing in yourself.”

Cisse went on to speak about the moment he found out he would be joining Milan during the January transfer window. He also had strong interest from Eredivisie side PSV at the time.

“My friends’ WhatsApp group exploded,” he recalled. “‘Alpha, is this true?,’ they were asking. And I said, ‘yeah guys, yes’. PSV wanted me immediately, but Milan were going to let me finish the season in Serie B. Two great teams, but Milan … you can’t describe it.

“It was a mix of emotions. My parents told me to stay calm and that the best was still yet to come. We decided that this was the right choice, and seeing how it’s going, I’d say we were right.”

PSV had been so close to signing Cisse, that he says he was “practically on the flight to Rotterdam to sign with PSV, but then Milan came in.”

Cisse’s first experiences with Milan came during the back end of the 2025-26 season, when he received treatment for an injury he picked up in Serie B.

“The first times I went to Milanello were for the injury recovery. Milan let me stay with Catanzaro, but I got injured a few days after. In fact, I had some big doubts: ‘I’m going to Milan after an injury, let’s see how it all goes’.

“This is exactly what Ruben Amorim spoke to me about when we first met. We focused on the injury, he explained what he wanted from me on the pitch. He’s a great person, who knows how to work with young people. And he knows how to keep my feet on the ground, even if I’m not one of those whose head is in the clouds.”

It has been a rapid rise to the top since then: Cisse is Milan’s leading goalscorer across all competitions with eight from 13 appearances, and their joint-top goalscorer in Serie A with five (from nine outings).

The first hat-trick of his career came in a 4-0 victory away against RB Salzburg in October.

“Everything felt clear to me after the hat-trick in the Europa League,” said Cisse. “It was confirmation of what I had thought to myself. It didn’t feel like I’d ‘arrived’, it was the realisation of a promise I’d made to myself as a child.

“Even though I was coming off a long injury, even though I’m young and still have a lot to improve, I’ve never had any doubts about my qualities and the places I could go. I’m very demanding of myself.

“My life has changed a lot over the last few months, maybe even more than I’ve realised myself. There are times when I stop and think about how different everything is compared to a short while ago. Football is taking me to places that I never could have dreamed of, but I’m still the same person inside.

“I know what my ambitions are and maybe that’s what helps me to not get lost in all of this, even when everything around you is changing.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

Very exciting young player. This is the way forward. Stop letting these talents go abroad for pennies. Give them opportunities here and now. Serie A needs more Cisse’s getting signed up and less examples like Issa Doumbia who all the bigs slept on and let get away. Last season alone really shows how much quality is in Serie B waiting to be given the chance to take the next step.

#1272. Inside Cristiano Ronaldo Jr's bid to step out of his father's shadow after his Portugal Under-17s call-up: From padel beef with Rio Ferdinand to a Coca-Cola BAN

Published: 02:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 05:50 EST, 9 November 2026

He has spent his whole life being measured against European football's greatest goalscorer. Now Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. has taken his biggest step yet.

The 16-year-old has been called up to Portugal's U17 squad for the first time, and will face Andorra on November 11 and Serbia on November 14. And the timing is hard to ignore.

The famous No. 7 shirt Ronaldo Sr wore for two decades will now be vacant after he announced his retirement from international football on Thursday.

It's a heavy shirt for anyone to inherit. Luis Figo graced the number when he led Portugal’s golden generation to the 2006 World Cup semi-finals, and Ronaldo Sr himself carried it when he captained them to the European Championship in 2016. Both won the Ballon d’Or and are two of the most tantalising players the nation has ever produced.

Portugal’s power vacuum is also a pressure point. As the son of the man who wore that shirt, Ronaldo Jr. will attract more attention, and more expectation.

The national team lacks its focal point, and few names carry more weight than his. He is the natural successor in marketing terms, if nothing else. Whether he is the player to take it is another matter.

Cristiano Ronaldo Jr - son of the Portuguese great - is looking to forge his own football career

This week the 16-year-old earned his first call-up to Portugal's U17 team

The weight of his father's expectations has been there from the start. Ronaldo Jr once floated the idea of becoming a goalkeeper, and his father’s reaction was swift. “No, I don’t want that! Are you joking or what?” Ronaldo Sr responds in the 2015 documentary Ronaldo.

Up front for the Juventus academy, his record would make the man chasing 1,000 career goals jealous: a staggering 58 goals in 23 games for the Under-9s. Yet his father was never satisfied. Asked at the 2020 Globe Soccer Awards, with his son sitting in the audience, whether the boy had what it takes to reach the top, Ronaldo Sr’s answer was blunt.

“Not yet,” he said. “I’m hard with him sometimes because he drinks Coca-Cola and Fanta. (He has) chips and fries; I fight with him.”

Hard data on his youth career since then is limited. Reports of his interest in switching to the Real Madrid academy suggested a desire to develop and compete.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Ronaldo Sr. at Manchester United, has seen that competitive streak in the son on the padel court.

“I was in the Red Sea a couple of days ago; I play padel every day. (When) me and Cristiano Jr. get mad, we don't speak for like two days.” He exclaimed on Five Presents. Like his father, he doesn’t take losing well.

His body, though, has settled the question of position. At 6 ft 3 in, he already stands taller than his father. Growth spurts may temporarily cost him some of the pace and the effortless coordination of his youth. A forced adaption of his style is not unusual: Ronaldo’s former teammates Gareth Bale and Scott McTominay were both moved into new positions to begin their professional careers.

It is also a path his father walked. Forget stepovers, flicks and trademark ‘Ronaldo chop’. Jr’s game is currently closer to the Ronaldo of Juventus and the Old Trafford return: a penalty-box predator who lives on timing and movement rather than dribbling past defenders.

The young striker has represented the youth academies of Man United, Real Madrid and Juventus

But his ultra-professional father said his son needs to cut out the Coca-Cola if he wants to make it at the top level

His Portugal numbers are respectable, not remarkable. Five goals in 13 appearances is a decent return, but he has played just 522 minutes, an average of around 40 per game, and scored roughly once every 104 minutes. However, it is a tiny sample size.

To reach the top, he will need the work ethic his father is famous for. “I’ve never seen a more professional person,” Paul Scholes, Ronaldo Sr’s former Manchester United teammate, told Premier League Productions. “He was out there all day long, practising … he had weights on his ankles.”

Habits like that are built in demanding environments, and Jr’s has been a gentle one.

Playing in Saudi Arabia still has its positives. As Jr. transitions from boy to man, weaker opposition has given him room to grow into his body and build confidence as he prepares for men's senior football. But that breathing space has a shelf life.

He has options. He could stay and share a dressing room with his father, or return to one of the academies of Ronaldo Sr’s former clubs, with Real Madrid, Juventus and Manchester United all reported by The Sun to be interested. He has the name, the call-up and the options, but not yet the proof.

When Ronaldo Sr walked away from Portugal, he left behind a shirt, a record and a question. Saudi Arabia cannot give his son the answer. If he wants international caps and Champions League football, he must leave Al Nassr and his old man for a stage where nobody gives him an inch.

The surname opened the door. Only he can walk through it.

#1271. Forget Hogh: 3 Celtic Players Are in Serious Danger of Being Exiled in January

Celtic have gone into the international break on the back of successive wins after their narrow and rather unglamorous win over Kilmarnock on Sunday.

The Bhoys came out on top thanks to a first-half goal from Liam Scales, and combined with Thursday night's Europa League win, they go into the break with a very different feeling from the last international window.

Back in September, Celtic went into the break on the back of three straight defeats, and Martin O'Neill was left contemplating his own future. The Bhoys now have a moment's rest from the criticism, but some players will be worried about their position in this squad.

Here we take a look at the players who are at risk of being cut by O'Neill in the January transfer window.

McCowan has had a tough season so far, and it all started with his disastrous cameo against LASK in that infamous Champions League collapse. The midfielder was slaughtered by fans after that game, and some of it crossed the line into abuse.

McCowan has come back into the fray a little of late, making two substitute appearances in the last two league games, but it doesn't feel as though O'Neill fully trusts him, and this is not a young player.

McCowan is 28 years of age and he cannot get into a team that has a particularly poor midfield and a clear lack of depth in the middle. That is an indictment in itself, and we have already seen reports that McCowan could be offloaded if Celtic can find a replacement.

The curious case of Mr Ralston. The right-back did well last season and even won World Cup spot with Scotland, but he has been missing since. Alistair Johnston has barely played, but it is Colby Donovan who has seized the opportunity to become the lead deputy,and to add insult to injury, Celtic went and signed another right-back in Jordan Lotomba, who has seen more starts than Ralston, who is yet to start.

Ralston does not have a single league appearance to his name, and he finds himself the fourth-choice right-back at this stage. He is out of contract in the summer, and it would be stunning if Celtic don't offload him in the winter window.

It would be best for both parties to move on, and it's clear that the right-back position is one of the few areas this Celtic squad actuall has enough depth.

Tounekti has had a tough time of things this season. He has been heavily criticised for his lack of consistency, and for his predictability as a winger. He is somewhere between unable and unwilling to repeatedly run at and beat his men, regularly turning inside or taking the easy option.

The Tunisia international has talent, there is little doubt, but he has been given repeated opportunities this season amid injury issues on the left, and he has repeatedly fallen short of expectations. In fact, in 17 appearances across all competitions, Tounekti has one assist and no goals. That's just not good enough for a winger who plays for a team that generally dominate opponents domestically. Being a winger for Celtic, especially under O'Neill's direct style. should be a dream.

Fans have run out of patience when it comes to Tounekti, and it feels as though O'Neill's patience is also wearing thin. To make matters worse for the winger, Jota and Yang Hyun-jun are now nearing full fitness, while Callum Osmand has also impressed on the left.

O'Neill may feel as though he has enough on that side, and if the right-footed Tounekti isn't going to compete on the other side, a loan move, in particular, could be seen as a good option.
